items.en: Who is Marcus's brother?

items.en: How many brothers does Julia have?
items.hint: a number in the nominative plural

items.en: What is the mother's name?

items.en: What is the father's name?
items.hint: three names in the nominative

items.en: How many names does a Roman man have?
items.hint: a number in the nominative plural, neuter to agree with nōmina

items.en: What is 'Lucius'?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the naming form)

items.en: What are 'Marcus' and 'Quintus'?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative plural

items.en: Is Aemilius with his sister?
items.hint: the sentence answers yes or no — choose the statement that agrees with it

items.en: Who is Aemilius?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the naming form)

items.en: Why is the mother sad?
choices: quod frāter eius mīles nōn est
items.hint: quod (because) + an object in the accusative, an infinitive and nōn potest

items.en: Where is the children's uncle?
items.hint: the place after in — the ablative

items.en: What is Aemilius?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the naming form)

items.en: What (who) is a soldier?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a relative clause (quī ... fert)

items.en: What are the arms of a Roman soldier?
items.hint: nouns in the nominative

items.q: Quid agunt mīlitēs Rōmānī in Germāniā?
items.en: What are the Roman soldiers doing in Germany?
items.hint: a verb in the third person plural

items.en: With what do boys fight?
items.hint: a noun in the ablative plural (the 'with' form) — not with arms

items.en: Surely Aemilius does not carry a spear as well?
items.hint: num expects the answer no

items.en: What (who) is a horseman?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a relative clause

items.q: Estne pīlum tam longum quam hasta?
items.en: Is a javelin as long as a spear?
items.hint: the sentence answers yes or no — choose the statement that agrees with it

items.q: Quot pedēs longum est pīlum Aemiliī?
items.en: How many feet long is Aemilius's javelin?
items.hint: a number (this one never changes its ending); pedēs is accusative

items.q: Quot pedēs longus est gladius Aemiliī?
items.en: How many feet long is Aemilius's sword?
items.hint: a number in the accusative, agreeing with pedēs

items.q: Cūr gladius peditis tam brevis est?
items.en: Why is the foot-soldier's sword so short?
choices: quod pedes gladium gravem ferre nōn potest
quod eques gladium brevem semper fert
items.hint: quod (because) + a comparison with tam ... quam

items.en: What is the horseman's sword like?
items.hint: comparative adjectives (-ior) in the nominative

items.en: Who are the Germans?
choices: mīlitēs Rōmānī quī in Germāniā sunt
items.hint: a noun in the nominative plural with an adjective and a relative clause

items.en: What is a province?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the naming form)

items.en: Surely Germany is not a Roman province?
items.hint: num expects the answer no

items.en: What separates Germany from Gaul?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the naming form)

items.en: What is the homeland of the Germans?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: What are the Germans (to the Romans)?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative plural with a genitive

items.en: What is an army?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a genitive plural

items.en: Who is the leader of the army?
items.hint: a relative clause: (is) quī ... dūcit

items.en: Whom does the army obey?
items.hint: a noun in the dative (the 'to' form) — pāret takes the dative

items.q: Cūr paucī mīlitēs Rōmānī in Hispāniā Galliāque sunt?
items.en: Why are there few Roman soldiers in Spain and Gaul?
items.hint: nam (for, because) + a clause with pārent and a dative

items.q: Quid ferunt Hispānī et Gallī quī in exercitibus Rōmānīs mīlitant?
items.en: What do the Spaniards and Gauls who serve in the Roman armies carry?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative plural (the object form)

items.en: Where does Aemilius live?
items.hint: in + the ablative plural

items.en: What is a camp?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a genitive plural

items.q: Quot mīlitēs in castrīs Aemiliī habitant?
items.en: How many soldiers live in Aemilius's camp?
items.hint: a number (mīlia) with a genitive plural

items.q: Cūr nūllae feminae aut puerī in castrīs habitant?
items.en: Why do no women or boys live in the camp?
answers: quod feminae et puerī mīlitāre nōn possunt
items.hint: enim or quia (because) + an infinitive with nōn possunt

items.en: What is around the camp?
items.hint: nouns in the nominative

items.q: Quot pedēs altum est vāllum castrōrum?
items.en: How many feet high is the rampart of the camp?
items.hint: a number (this one never changes its ending); pedēs is accusative

items.en: How many gates does the camp have?
items.hint: a number (this one never changes its ending)

items.q: Quālis est via inter duās portās?
items.en: What is the road between the two gates like?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative, agreeing with via

items.en: When are the gates of the camp closed?
items.hint: the time after in — the ablative

items.en: Can the enemy take the Roman camp?
items.hint: the sentence answers yes or no — choose the statement that agrees with it

items.en: Where do the terrified barbarians flee to?
items.hint: in + the accusative plural (motion into)

items.q: Fugitne mīles Rōmānus ab hoste armātō?
items.en: Does a Roman soldier flee from an armed enemy?
items.hint: the sentence answers yes or no — choose the statement that agrees with it

items.en: What are the Roman soldiers like?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative plural, agreeing with mīlitēs

items.en: Aren't the Germans brave?
items.hint: nōnne expects the answer yes — Julius adds a comparison

items.en: What is the Germans' shield like?
items.hint: nimis (too) + an adjective in the nominative, neuter to agree with scūtum

items.en: What is our javelin like?
items.hint: adjectives in the nominative, neuter to agree with pīlum

items.en: Who can take Rome?
items.hint: a word in the nominative meaning 'no (enemy)'

items.en: Why don't the Romans conquer Germany?
answers: quod Germānia montibus, silvīs et flūminibus dēfenditur
items.hint: quod (because) + the passive dēfenditur with ablatives (the means)
